title: 동네 · 이웃
intro: 집 주제와 짝으로 자주 나오는 단골 주제로, 동네 묘사 → 동네에서 하는 일 → 동네의 변화 → 어릴 때 동네와 비교 순서로 출제됩니다. 모든 답변은 '회사 근처 조용한 주거 지역, 지하철역 5분, 편의점·카페·작은 공원, 한강까지 자전거 10분'이라는, 3년째 혼자 사는 하나의 동네로 통일하세요. 공원 산책·한강 조깅·카페 독서 이야기가 그대로 공원·조깅·카페 주제 답변으로 재활용되고, 비교 질문에는 대학 때까지 살던 대전 동네를 씁니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Okay, let me tell you about my neighborhood.' → 동네 기본 정보(조용한 주거 지역, 회사 근처) → 주변 시설(지하철역·편의점·카페·공원·한강) → 좋아하는 점과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
위치는 거리·시간으로 구체적으로 말하세요: 'It's a five-minute walk to the subway station.' / 'It takes ten minutes by bike.'
혼자 사는 직장인 시점으로 '퇴근길에 들르는 편의점', '주말 아침 카페', '저녁 한강 조깅'처럼 내 생활과 연결하면 IH 이상이 됩니다.
변화·비교 질문은 '3년 전 처음 이사 왔을 때 vs 지금', '대전에서 자란 동네 vs 지금 서울 동네'로 차이 2가지와 느낌을 말합니다.

expressions.en: Okay, let me tell you about my neighborhood.
expressions.ko: 네, 우리 동네에 대해 말해 볼게요.

expressions.en: I live in a quiet residential area.
It's a five-minute walk to the subway station.
There's a convenience store right next to my building.
expressions.ko: 우리 건물 바로 옆에 편의점이 있어요.

expressions.en: There are a lot of nice cafes around here.
There's a small park near my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트 근처에 작은 공원이 있어요.

expressions.en: It only takes ten minutes to get to the Han River by bike.
My neighborhood is really safe, even at night.
What I like most about my neighborhood is that it's so convenient.
expressions.ko: 우리 동네에서 제일 좋은 점은 정말 편리하다는 거예요.
expressions.note: What I like most about ~ is that ~

expressions.en: I often stop by the convenience store on my way home from work.
expressions.note: stop by: 잠깐 들르다 / on my way home: 집에 가는 길에

expressions.en: It's close to my office, but it doesn't feel busy at all.
expressions.ko: 회사와 가깝지만 전혀 복잡하게 느껴지지 않아요.

expressions.en: A lot has changed since I first moved here.
expressions.ko: 처음 이사 왔을 때 이후로 많은 게 바뀌었어요.

expressions.en: So yeah, that's why I really like my neighborhood.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 저는 우리 동네가 정말 좋아요.

expressions.en: It's the perfect mix of city life and peace and quiet.
expressions.ko: 도시 생활과 한적함이 완벽하게 섞여 있어요.

expressions.en: It didn't take long for this place to feel like home.
expressions.ko: 이곳이 집처럼 느껴지기까지 오래 걸리지 않았어요.
expressions.note: It didn't take long for A to ~: A가 ~하는 데 오래 걸리지 않았다

questions.en: Tell me about your neighborhood. What does it look like, and what is there around your home?
questions.ko: 사는 동네에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떻게 생겼고, 집 주변에는 무엇이 있나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 동네 기본 정보(조용한 주거 지역, 회사 근처) → 지하철역·편의점·카페·공원·한강 → 좋아하는 점과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'It's a five-minute walk to ~', 'right next to ~'로 위치를 구체적으로 말하세요.
시설을 나열만 하지 말고 '퇴근길에 들른다'처럼 내가 그곳을 어떻게 이용하는지 한 줄씩 붙이세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my neighborhood. I live near my office in Seoul. It's a quiet residential area. The subway station is a five-minute walk from my apartment. There's a convenience store right next to my building. There are also a lot of nice cafes. There's a small park near my apartment, too. And it only takes ten minutes to get to the Han River by bike. Yeah, that's my neighborhood.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about my neighborhood. I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul, close to my office. I moved here about three years ago, when I started my job. It's really convenient. The subway station is just a five-minute walk from my apartment, so my commute is easy. There's a convenience store right next to my building, and I often stop by on my way home from work. There are also a lot of nice cafes around here. On weekends, I like reading a book at one of them with an iced americano. There's a small park near my place, too, and I take walks there in the evening. Plus, it only takes ten minutes to get to the Han River by bike. What I like most is that it's close to work, but it doesn't feel busy at all. Yeah, that's why I really like my neighborhood.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about my neighborhood. I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul, not far from my office. I moved here about three years ago when I got my job, and honestly, it didn't take long for this place to feel like home. The best part is how convenient everything is. The subway station is just a five-minute walk away, so my commute is super easy. There's a convenience store right next to my building, and I stop by almost every night on my way home for a snack or some milk. The streets are lined with small cafes, and on weekend mornings, you can usually find me at my favorite one, reading a book with an iced americano. There's also a little park a few minutes from my place. It's nothing fancy, just some trees, benches, and a walking path, but it's perfect for an evening walk after a long day. And if I want more space, the Han River is only ten minutes away by bike. That's where I go jogging a few times a week. Even though it's close to a busy business area, my street is really calm, especially at night. It's the perfect mix of city life and peace and quiet. Yeah, that's why I really like my neighborhood.

questions.en: What do you usually do in your neighborhood on weekends? Where do you go, and who do you go with?
questions.ko: 주말에 동네에서 주로 무엇을 하나요? 어디에 가고, 누구와 함께 가나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 토요일 아침(카페) → 오후(공원·장보기) → 저녁(친구들과 맛집) → 일요일(한강) → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
혼자 하는 것(카페 독서·산책)과 친구와 하는 것(맛집·한강)을 나눠 말하면 자연스럽게 길어집니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about my weekends. On Saturday mornings, I usually sleep in. Then I go to a cafe near my apartment. I read a book there with an iced americano. In the afternoon, I take a walk in the small park. Sometimes I go grocery shopping. In the evening, I meet my friends. We go to a nice restaurant in my neighborhood. On Sundays, I ride a bike to the Han River. Yeah, that's my weekend.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my weekends. Since I'm busy with work during the week, I like to take it easy on weekends. On Saturday mornings, I usually sleep in until ten. Then I walk to my favorite cafe near my apartment. I order an iced americano and read a book there for a couple of hours. It's my little me time. In the afternoon, I take a walk in the small park near my place, or I go grocery shopping for the week. On Saturday evenings, I often meet my friends in my neighborhood. We try new restaurants, because a lot of new places open around here. On Sundays, if the weather is nice, I ride a bike to the Han River. It only takes ten minutes. Sometimes Minji joins me, and we get fried chicken by the river. Yeah, that's what I usually do on weekends.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about my weekends. Since my weekdays are packed with meetings, I try to keep my weekends slow and easy, and most of the time, I don't even leave my neighborhood. On Saturdays, I sleep in until about ten. Then I walk over to my favorite cafe, which is just around the corner. I always get an iced americano, find a seat by the window, and get lost in a book for a couple of hours. Honestly, that's my favorite part of the whole week. In the afternoon, I take a walk in the little park near my place or pick up groceries for the week. Saturday evenings are for my friends. There are tons of new restaurants popping up around here, so we usually pick one and spend hours eating and catching up. On Sundays, if the weather is nice, I hop on a bike and ride to the Han River, which only takes about ten minutes. My coworker Minji often comes along. We sit on the grass, order some fried chicken, and just watch the sunset. It's a simple routine, but it really recharges me for the week ahead. Yeah, that's what my weekends usually look like.

questions.en: Has your neighborhood changed since you first moved there? Tell me about a memorable change. What happened, and how did it affect you?
questions.ko: 처음 이사 왔을 때 이후로 동네가 바뀌었나요? 기억에 남는 변화에 대해 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 나에게 어떤 영향을 주었나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 처음 이사 왔을 때 모습(3년 전) → 기억에 남는 변화(공원 리모델링) → 나에게 준 영향 → 느낌 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'When I first moved here, ~'(과거) → 'Now, ~'(현재) / 'A lot has changed since ~'(현재완료)로 시제를 구분하세요.
변화의 좋은 점 하나, 아쉬운 점 하나를 같이 말하면 IH 이상의 답변이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, my neighborhood? Let me think. Yes, it has changed a lot. I moved here about three years ago. Back then, the small park near my apartment was old and dark. Last year, the city fixed it up. Now there's a new walking path and a lot of lights. There are also new benches and flowers. I take a walk there almost every evening. I feel safe at night, too. Yeah, that's the biggest change in my neighborhood.
answers.IH: Oh, my neighborhood? Let me think. Yes, a lot has changed since I first moved here about three years ago. The most memorable change is the small park near my apartment. When I first moved here, it was pretty old and dark. There were only a few broken benches, and I never went there at night. But last year, the city fixed it up. It took about four months. Now there's a new walking path, a lot of bright lights, and pretty flowers everywhere. The change really affected my daily life. Now I take a walk there almost every evening after work, and I feel safe even at night. It's also a great place to cool down after jogging. The only bad thing is that it's a lot more crowded now. Yeah, that's the biggest change in my neighborhood.
answers.AL: Oh, my neighborhood? Let me think. Yeah, a lot has changed since I first moved here about three years ago, but one change really stands out. It's the little park near my apartment. When I first moved in, honestly, it was kind of sad. The benches were old and broken, there were hardly any lights, and I always walked around it at night instead of going through it. Then last spring, the city started fixing it up. For about four months, there was just noisy construction, and I was getting pretty annoyed. But when it finally reopened, I was blown away. There was a brand-new walking path, bright lights everywhere, and flower beds along the edges. It completely changed my evenings. Since I live alone, I used to just go straight home after work and stay on the sofa. Now I take a walk there almost every night, and it's become my favorite way to clear my head after a long day. I even see the same neighbors walking their dogs, so it feels more like a community now. The only downside is that it gets pretty crowded on weekends. Yeah, that's the change in my neighborhood that I'm most thankful for.

questions.en: How is the neighborhood you live in now different from the one you grew up in?
questions.ko: 지금 사는 동네는 자란 동네와 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 자란 동네(대전, 오래된 아파트 단지) → 지금 동네(서울, 회사 근처) → 차이점 2가지(편리함, 이웃과의 관계) → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'used to + 동사원형'으로 예전 습관을, 'On the other hand, ~'로 대조를 표현하세요.
한쪽만 칭찬하지 말고 각각의 장점을 인정하면 수준 높은 답변이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a good question. I grew up in Daejeon. My family lived in an old apartment complex there. It was a quiet area with a big playground. I knew all my neighbors. Now, I live alone in Seoul, near my office. My neighborhood now is more convenient. There's a subway station, a lot of cafes, and a park nearby. But I don't really know my neighbors. Yeah, that's the difference between my two neighborhoods.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a good question. I grew up in Daejeon, and my family lived in an old apartment complex there until I finished college. It was a quiet area with a big playground, a small market, and lots of trees. Everyone knew each other, so the neighbors used to say hi and give us fruit. My neighborhood in Seoul is pretty different. First, it's much more convenient. The subway station is a five-minute walk away, and there are tons of cafes and restaurants. In Daejeon, we had to take a bus to go almost anywhere. Second, people here are busier. Most people in my building live alone and work like me, so I don't really know my neighbors. Sometimes I miss that warm feeling. But for my life now, Seoul is a better fit. Yeah, that's how the two neighborhoods are different.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a good question. I grew up in Daejeon, and my family lived in the same old apartment complex until I finished college, so I have a lot of memories there. It was a quiet area with a big playground, a small traditional market, and tall trees everywhere. What I remember most is how close everyone was. The lady next door used to bring us fruit, and my brother Junho and I played outside with the neighborhood kids until dinner. My neighborhood in Seoul is a whole different story. First of all, it's way more convenient. The subway station is a five-minute walk away, there's a convenience store right next to my building, and I can find a nice cafe on almost every corner. Back in Daejeon, we had to take a bus just to get to a decent cafe. On the other hand, people here keep to themselves. Most people in my building are office workers who live alone, like me, so we just nod at each other in the elevator. To be honest, I sometimes miss that small-town warmth. But for this stage of my life, my neighborhood in Seoul is a much better fit. Yeah, that's how my two neighborhoods are different.

pronunciation.tip: '네이버후드'. 첫 음절 '네이'에 강세, gh는 소리 나지 않아요
'컨비니언트'. v는 윗니로 아랫입술을 살짝 물고, '비'에 강세
'리버'. r은 혀를 말고 시작, v는 윗니를 아랫입술에 대고 진동
